description: Three real clean/broken capture pairs for the EVALUATE-stage Diff-the-Trace assessment. The discriminating byte in each pair is the dissector's computed divergence over real bytes — never an answer key.

provenance.captured_with: tcpdump -i eth0 inside docker (ubuntu:24.04, --cap-add=NET_RAW): port-443 + port-80 legs driven by `curl https://www.google.com` and `curl http://neverssl.com`; ARP legs forced by flushing the neighbour cache and pinging in-subnet hosts.
provenance.pcaps: eth.pcap (clean 443/TLS), http.pcap (real cleartext :80 GET), arp.pcap (real request/reply)
provenance.cross_checked_against: tshark 4.x: Pair A clean dst-port 443 / broken dst-port 80; Pair B clean TLS ContentType 0x17-class record / broken cleartext 'GET / HTTP/1.1' start-line on :80; Pair C clean ARP request (opcode 1) / broken ARP reply (opcode 2).
provenance.honesty_note: Every leg is real bytes. The 'broken' legs are genuine instances: a real port-80 SYN, a real cleartext HTTP GET, a real ARP reply. Pair C's 'unsolicited' framing is the presentation scope (an opcode-2 reply shown without its paired request — exactly the on-wire shape of gratuitous ARP); the bytes are an unmodified real reply. The dissector computes the divergence; the puzzle is generated from it.

clean.label: TLS application-protected record
clean.note: the TLS record byte 0 is a TLS ContentType (0x16 here; 0x17=application_data is the encrypted-payload class) — opaque on the wire

broken.label: cleartext HTTP GET on 80
broken.note: the TCP payload starts 47 45 54 = 'GET' — a readable application start-line, the opposite of in-transit confidentiality

broken.label: ARP reply with no paired request (gratuitous-shape)
